big_case.notes: Pro se debtor's emergency stay/injunction application seeking to halt a single E.D. Va. bankruptcy appeal following a § 455(a) recusal denial and a December 17, 2026 residential foreclosure sale while Fourth Circuit rehearing of a mandamus denial remained pending. High personal stakes for one household, but virtually zero doctrinal, institutional, or public significance, underscored by routine three-day solo chambers denial without response, referral, amici, or writing.

leakage.notes: Prediction ran in forward mode on 2026-11-14T03:56–04:10Z, two days before Chief Justice Roberts denied 26A684 on 2026-11-16. Retrieval log (58 calls, outcome_only capture) shows reads of provisioned inputs, corpus prior queries (including pre-snapshot sibling denials 26A657 on 2026-11-10 and 26A658 on 2026-11-11), and CourtListener lower-court/precedent checks; no web searches, no reads of data/qp-topics/, and no post-resolution material.

central_claims.claim: Chief Justice Roberts, acting alone in chambers without referring Application No. 26A684 to the full Court, will deny the application in a single-line order ('Application (26A684) denied by The Chief Justice.') without granting an administrative stay or substantive relief.

central_claims.basis: Chief Justice Roberts entered a standard one-line unexplained chambers denial with no opinion staged in record/opinion/, so the staged record does not disclose chambers' doctrinal reasoning.
central_claims.claim: Doctrinally, emergency relief is unwarranted under Hollingsworth and Nken because remedies remain pending below under Rule 23.3, mandamus over 28 U.S.C. § 455(a) recusal lacks cert prospects, and enjoining BOKF's foreclosure reaches beyond the recusal-mandamus order.
